referents.why: 'say to him' is third masculine singular, the one spoken to in the message: Pharaoh.
referents.category: object of the instruction to speak

referents.why: 'my people' is first common singular inside the quoted message 'thus says the LORD', so the speaker of that message is the LORD (the one quoted).
'that they may serve me' is first common singular in the same quoted message, so 'me' is the LORD.
'rise early' is a command spoken by the LORD to Moses; the implied you is Moses.
'present yourself before Pharaoh' is a command to Moses in the same outer speech.
'you will say to him' is spoken to Moses as the one who delivers the message.
'let my people go' is a command inside the quoted message, addressed to Pharaoh (second person masculine singular, the one the message is delivered to).
'that they may serve me' has a plural subject; the people is a collective noun taking plural agreement, the ones the release is for.

links.why: a link from the setting clause back to the LORD's opening clause is backward; the setting is inside the speech.
links.category: backward then link into speech frame

links.why: two commands joined by waw at one level, same person.
the weqatal 'you will say' continues whatever it follows, the participle setting the time.
a command followed by waw and a yiqtol in a different person is a purpose, not a plain 'and'.
the command 'let my people go' is followed by waw and a yiqtol in the third person, stating what it is for.
the saying clause 'he said' introduces commands that Moses is to hear.
links.category: speech content link to command group

links.why: 'you will say to him' is a saying clause introducing the message 'thus he says the LORD'.
'thus he says the LORD' introduces a command, 'let my people go', with its purpose; what is said is the imperative group.
links.category: speech content link to command group

groups.why: the LORD speaks to Moses: the commands, the setting, and the instruction to speak are its parts; the delivered message is a nested turn.
rise early and present yourself are commands joined by 'and' at one level: one imperative group, with two command members.
groups.category: commands joined by and as one group

groups.why: Moses is told to say to Pharaoh the message quoted from the LORD: a middle turn with Moses as the sender.
the innermost turn is the quoted message: its sender is the LORD, the one quoted, and its addressee is Pharaoh.
'let my people go' is the command; 'that they may serve me' is what qualifies it, its aim.

none_fit.what: a bare participle clause ('when Pharaoh goes out to the water') giving the time of the command that follows; no link type states a temporal setting.

cant_tell.what: whether the setting cl3 and cl4 belong to the LORD's words or to Moses's delivery
cant_tell.why: the second person and the sequence put them in the LORD's speech to Moses, so they are parts of the outer turn; recorded because the setting could be read as Moses's own timing.
